headline: Puppet and Roller hit active exploitation while NGINX patches a decade-old HTTP/2 flaw
standfirst: Two remote-code-execution flaws are being exploited in the wild, one of them now in CISA's KEV catalog; a ten-year-old NGINX HTTP/2 overflow gets fixes; a Java decoder bug is real but gated on specific silicon; and third-party scripts, a hijacked PyPI package and an unexplained federal network outage fill out the day.
bodyMarkdown:
## Actively exploited

CISA added Perforce Puppet Enterprise's deserialization flaw, CVE-2026-115731, to the KEV catalog citing reports of active exploitation. NVD scores it 9.4 Critical under CVSS 4.0, and the mechanics matter more than the number: any client holding a CA-signed agent certificate can execute code on the Puppet Server as its service user by submitting a crafted rich-data report over PUT. Where the certificate authority autosigns requests without strong verification, an unauthenticated network attacker can first obtain such a certificate — so exposure depends on CA configuration, not just patching cadence. Supplied vulnerable ranges cover Puppet 8.0.0 up to 8.22.2 and 9.0.0 up to 9.1.3, and Puppet Enterprise 2023.8.0 up to 2023.8.13, 2025.0.0 up to 2025.12.1, plus 2026.0.0. CISA's required action is to apply mitigations per vendor instructions under its risk-based patching directive, with a federal remediation due date attached; ransomware use is listed as unknown, so treat that as an open question rather than a clean bill. [[s32]]

Apache has confirmed in-the-wild exploitation of CVE-2026-129448, a 9.8 Critical unauthenticated deserialization in Roller's XML-RPC endpoint that reaches code execution because vendor extension types are deserialized before the requester is authenticated. Affected versions are 4.0.0 through 6.1.4; the record notes this is the same vulnerability as CVE-2026-82384, which had listed only 6.1.5 as affected — a scoping correction worth flagging to anyone who triaged off the earlier ID. Upgrade to 6.1.6 or later is the real fix; interim workarounds are setting `enabledForExtensions` to false or removing the `/roller-services/xmlrpc` servlet mapping and restarting. Disabling XML-RPC in the admin UI is explicitly not sufficient, because older versions deserialize before that check. [[s5]] The KEV catalog returns a confirmed miss for this CVE, which — as ever — says nothing about exploitation and everything about catalog timing.

## Vulnerabilities

NGINX's "nginx2root" bug, CVE-2026-123007, is the day's most uncomfortable read: a heap buffer overflow in HTTP/2 processing where the flow-control window can exceed its threshold, present since 1.9.5 and fixed in 1.31.9 and 1.30.7. CVSS 4.0 puts it at 9.2 Critical, network-reachable with no privileges or interaction, but with high attack complexity — the reliable outcomes are worker crashes and memory corruption, with code execution contingent on ASLR being disabled or bypassable. It is data-plane only, with no control plane exposure, and there is no KEV listing. Internet-facing HTTP/2 terminators are the population that matters here. [[s3]]

CVE-2026-114938, marketed as Java4Shell, is a High-severity (8.1 CVSS 3.1) out-of-bounds write in HotSpot's Base64 handling, reported by researchers to affect Java 17.0.6 and later, with the vulnerable path running only on x86-64 chips supporting AVX-512 VBMI. Oracle's affected-version list spans specific builds across Java SE 8, 17, 21, 25 and 27 plus GraalVM editions. The disclosure names Jira, Jenkins, Keycloak and three other applications as reachable targets. Analysis: the combination of high attack complexity, a hardware feature gate and no supplied report of exploitation makes this a patch-queue item rather than an emergency — but the hardware prerequisite is a poor filter, since AVX-512-capable servers are exactly the ones running build and identity infrastructure. No KEV listing is supplied. [[s21]]

## Breaches

At least 178 top web destinations served malware to visitors over a 24-hour window via a security vulnerability involving Optimizely's customization and testing platform, with named sites including the BBC, CNN, Equifax and Ledger. No CVE or root-cause detail was supplied; what is clear is the shape of the failure — a vendor script trusted across many properties became a delivery channel, and the testing tooling meant to vary experiences varied them toward exploits. [[s39]]

Microsoft's agent-framework package on PyPI was compromised to ship versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2, published 33 minutes apart, designed to run a credential stealer on every Python start and aimed at Azure, Azure DevOps and GitHub Actions secrets. Eight separate research teams are credited with the reporting, which suggests independent confirmation rather than a single vendor claim. Any build agent that installed during that window should be assumed to have leaked its cloud and CI credentials. [[s37]]

Day two of interruptions to the NSA's classified internal network brought staggered arrivals and logins at Fort Meade, while a source said classified national security work continued unimpeded. No cause, attribution or scope has been supplied; treat the outage as unexplained rather than as a detected intrusion. [[s7]]

## Research

Mandiant and Google's threat intelligence group have traced how the group tracked as Cold Relic — described as Russia-linked, formerly COLDRIVER and UNC4057 — turned a single stolen Google Workspace data cache into impersonation activity and a second U.S. organization's compromise, via linked third-party intrusions investigated from a 2026 victim. The reusable part is the playbook: one cloud compromise became a trust bridge rather than a terminus. [[s38]]

selected.title: Critical Apache Roller RCE Flaw Under Active Exploitation, No Authentication Required
selected.excerpt: A critical security flaw in Apache Roller, an open-source, Java-based blogging platform, has come under active exploitation in the wild, according to the Apache Software Foundation (ASF) The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-129448 (CVSS score: 9.8), is a case of unauthenticated deserialization in the XML-RPC endpoint that could lead to remote code execution. "Deserialization of Untrusted

nvd.description:
Deserialization of Untrusted Data in Apache Roller versions 4.0.0 through 6.1.4 allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code. The XML-RPC endpoint accepts vendor extension types and deserializes them before authenticating the requester.

This is the same vulnerability as CVE-2026-82384, which listed only Apache Roller 6.1.5 as affected. This issue is being actively exploited.

Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.6 or later, which disables the extension types and rejects XML-RPC requests when the XML-RPC feature is disabled.

Users who cannot upgrade right away should set "enabledForExtensions" to "false" in WEB-INF/web.xml, or remove the "/roller-services/xmlrpc" servlet mapping, and restart Roller. Disabling XML-RPC in the administration UI is not enough, because older versions deserialize the request before checking that setting.

selected.angle: Apache confirms in-the-wild exploitation of unauthenticated XML-RPC deserialization RCE (CVE-2026-129448, CVSS 9.8) in Roller 4.0.0–6.1.4, with upgrade to 6.1.6 or servlet removal as the only real fix.

selected.title: 10-Year-Old NGINX HTTP/2 Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Code on Servers
selected.excerpt: A flaw in NGINX's HTTP/2 support can allow an attacker to run code on servers with HTTP/2 enabled, without needing to log in. The decade-old flaw, CVE-2026-123007, dubbed "nginx2root," has been present in NGINX's open-source code since version 1.9.5, released on September 22, 2015. Fixed versions 1.31.9 and 1.30.7 came out today. F5, the company behind NGINX, says attackers can run code where

nvd.description:
This issue affects NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source configurations that use HTTP/2. When NGINX processes undisclosed traffic, the flow control window can exceed the allowed threshold, potentially resulting in a heap buffer overflow typically followed by an NGINX worker segmentation fault. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact: An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to crash the NGINX worker process, corrupt its memory, or potentially execute code remotely. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

selected.angle: A decade-old NGINX HTTP/2 heap overflow (CVE-2026-123007, CVSS 9.2) is fixed in 1.31.9 and 1.30.7 today; no KEV listing, but internet-facing data-plane servers need to move fast.

kev.shortDescription: Perforce Puppet Enterprise contains a deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability in Puppet’s report-processing code that allows a client with any CA-signed agent certificate to execute arbitrary code on the Puppet Server as the service user by submitting a report containing a crafted rich-data type through a PUT request. If the certificate authority automatically signs requests without strong verification, an unauthenticated network attacker can obtain a valid certificate and exploit the vulnerability.
kev.requiredAction: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.

nvd.description: Deserialization of untrusted data in the report-processing code of Puppet, as used by Puppet Server, in the affected releases, allows a client that holds any CA-signed agent certificate to execute arbitrary code on the Puppet Server as its service user by submitting a report containing a crafted rich-data type via PUT request. Where the certificate authority autosigns requests without strong verification, an unauthenticated network attacker can obtain such a certificate.

nvd.description: Vulnerability in the Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition product of Oracle Java SE (component: Compiler).  Supported versions that are affected are Oracle Java SE: 8u511b33-perf, 17.0.21.0.3, 21.0.13.0.3, 25.0.5.0.3, 27.0.1.0.3; Oracle GraalVM for JDK: 17.0.21.0.3 and  21.0.13.0.3; Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition: 21.3.20.0.3. Difficult to exploit vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker with network access via multiple protocols to compromise Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in takeover of Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition. Note: This vulnerability can only be exploited by supplying data to APIs in the specified Component without using Untrusted Java Web Start applications or Untrusted Java applets, such as through a web service. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 8.1 (Confidentiality, Integrity and Availability impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H).
